newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-H.Smith says profit hinges on housing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-H.Smith says profit hinges on housing.

text.p: Shipping, engineering and hardware group Howard Smith Ltd said on Tuesday that its ability to improve earnings in the year to June 30, 1997 would depend on the timing and strength of an expected recovery of the Australian housing sector in calendar 1997.

"Some recovery is expected (for the Australian housing market) in the calendar 1997 year," the company said after releasing annual results. "However, its timing and strength will have a significant influence on the group's ability to improve earnings in the current year," it said.
Howard Smith said it expected the Australian housing market downturn to continue at least until the end of calendar 1996.
"All other group activities, with the exception of shipping, are expected to report higher earnings," the company said.
Howard Smith earlier said its net profit for the year to June 30, 1996 rose 11.8 percent to A$86.13 million.
The company lifted its final dividend to 19 cents a share from 17.5 cents a share in the previous year.

The company said sales from its hardware distribution business, BBC Hardware Ltd, were down 3.2 percent to A$1.06 billion but its profit before goodwill amortisation, at A$60.6 million, was in line with the previous year.
"A reduction in trade sales was offset by improved retail sales growth generated by the agressive roll-out of the Hardwarehouse stores," Howard Smith said.
Howard Smith said strong earnings contributions from Hardwarehouse stores were expected to continue.

The company said higher sales from its industrial supplies division, Blackwoods, were offset by reduced sales from its engineering firm, Goninan, due to the end of a contract to supply rail stock to the New South Wales State Railway Authority.

"Sales demand (for industrial supplies) is expected to remain steady in the year underpinned by orders from major supply contracts and emerging sales from new branches. Earnings are expected to be above last year," the company said.
The company said Goninan's contract to supply locomotives and other rolling stock to the National Rail Corp were expected to provide strong momentum for the earnings for in 1996/97.
Operating earnings from the company's shipping group were expected to be lower than in 1995/96 as it wound down operations with the contracted sale of its two remaining tankers.

Howard Smith said its marine and towage operations in Australia and the U.K. were expected to be higher than the previous year due to new towage assets in Australia and cost rationalisations in the U.K.
